title: Gangnam, Seoul: A Beginner's Guide to Korea's Most Famous District
html:
If you've heard one Korean place name before visiting Korea, it's probably Gangnam — thanks to Psy's 2012 hit "Gangnam Style." The real Gangnam is a huge district on the south side of the Han River in Seoul, and it's one of the easiest areas for first-time visitors to explore because almost everything connects by subway. Here's what it actually is, how to get around it, and what's worth your time.

What Is Gangnam, Exactly?

Gangnam-gu ("-gu" just means "district") is one of Seoul's 25 districts, and it's known for office towers, high-end shopping, and a fast-paced lifestyle — a bit like a mix of a business district and an entertainment district. Confusingly, "Gangnam" also refers more narrowly to the neighborhood right around Gangnam Station, which is the busiest part of the district. The sights in this guide are spread across a few different neighborhoods inside Gangnam-gu, so don't expect them all to be within walking distance of each other.

Getting to Gangnam

The easiest way in is Subway Line 2 (the green line) to Gangnam Station — it's one of the busiest subway stations in the country, so expect crowds, especially on weekday evenings. Buy a T-money card (sold at any convenience store near a subway station) and top it up with cash; it works on every subway and bus in Seoul, so you won't need to buy a new paper ticket every ride.

Because the different attractions below sit in different neighborhoods, you'll usually need to hop back on the subway (or take a short taxi ride) to move between them rather than walking the whole area in one go.

Gangnam Station Area: Shopping, Cafes, and Nightlife

Right above and below Gangnam Station is a dense grid of clothing shops, cosmetic stores, and cafes, plus an underground shopping arcade that connects several subway exits — handy on a rainy or freezing day. In the evening, the streets around Exit 10 and Exit 11 fill up with restaurants, bars, and "coin karaoke" booths (tiny one- or two-song karaoke rooms you pay for by the song, no reservation needed). A local habit worth copying: Koreans usually agree to meet "underground near Exit 11" rather than above ground, since it's easier to find each other out of the wind, rain, or summer heat.

COEX Mall and Bongeunsa Temple

A couple of subway stops from Gangnam Station (get off at Samseong Station instead) is COEX, one of the largest underground malls in the world, home to the famous Starfield Library and a large aquarium. It's worth a whole visit on its own — we've covered it in detail in separate guides to COEX Mall and the COEX Artium theater inside it.

Right across the street from COEX is Bongeunsa Temple, a working Buddhist temple that's been there since the Silla dynasty, long before any of the skyscrapers around it. It's free to walk through, and the contrast between the quiet temple grounds and the glass towers just outside the gate is one of the more memorable sights in Seoul. Visitors are welcome, but it's still an active place of worship, so keep your voice down and dress modestly (covered shoulders and knees).

K-Star Road and Apgujeong: For K-Pop Fans

If you're into K-pop, head to K-Star Road, a street near Apgujeong Rodeo Station (on the Bundang Line — you'll need to transfer from Line 2, or just take a taxi) lined with cartoon bear statues called "GangnamDols," each decorated for a different K-pop group. The exact statues and their positions change from time to time as new groups debut, so think of it as a fun photo walk rather than a fixed checklist. The walk from one end to the other takes about 20–30 minutes, and it connects to Garosu-gil, a tree-lined street popular for boutique shopping and brunch cafes.

Practical Tips for First-Time Visitors

  • Gangnam is one of the pricier areas in Seoul for food and coffee — expect to pay somewhat more here than in neighborhoods like Hongdae or Itaewon.
  • It's very safe to walk around at night, including alone; the area is well-lit and busy until late.
  • Casual clothing is fine everywhere except inside Bongeunsa Temple, where modest dress is appreciated.
  • Most shops and restaurants take credit cards, but it's smart to carry a little cash for small cafes or street food stalls.

💬 Been to Gangnam, or planning your first trip there? Drop your questions in the comments below — happy to help!
meta_description: A beginner's guide to Gangnam, Seoul: how to get there, COEX, Bongeunsa Temple, K-Star Road, and practical first-timer tips.
